title: Come and see (John 1:29–39)
hook: John points, two disciples follow, and Jesus asks what seek you

segments.voice: Yesterday, eskenosen: the Word was made flesh, and pitched his tent among us. Your line was and dwelt among us.

Bethania, beyond the Jordan. John is baptizing there when he sees a man walking toward him, and he points. What he says next is a line the priest repeats at Mass just before Communion, lifting the host: behold the Lamb of God. It didn't come from a council or a liturgist. It came from a riverbank. Today, that line, and what two people do the moment they hear it.
screen: `BETHANIA, BEYOND THE JORDAN.` → `A MAN WALKING TOWARD HIM.` → `A LINE NOW SAID AT MASS.`

segments.voice: John the Baptist sees Jesus coming and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world." Lamb of God is a strange thing to call a man. Readers hear in it the Passover lamb, whose blood marked the doors in Egypt, the lambs offered every day in the temple, and Isaiah's servant, led as a sheep to the slaughter. John packs all of that into one name. The next day he says it again, and two of his own disciples hear him, leave him, and follow Jesus. Jesus turns, sees them trailing behind, and speaks his first words in this Gospel: "What seek you?" Not who are you, not what do you believe. What are you looking for? They answer with a question of their own: Rabbi, where do you live? And he says: "Come and see." No sermon, no test, just an invitation to come along and look. They came, saw where he abode, and stayed with him that day; John even remembers the hour, about the tenth hour, late in the afternoon. One of the two was Andrew. The other is never named; some readers have thought it was the writer himself, remembering the afternoon his life turned. The Church keeps John's pointing finger at the center of the Mass. The Lamb of God is sung while the bread is broken, and then the priest lifts the host, points as John pointed, and says: behold.
screen: `JOHN POINTS: BEHOLD THE LAMB.` · `PASSOVER, TEMPLE, ISAIAH.` · `WHAT SEEK YOU?` · `COME AND SEE.`

segments.voice: Imagine someone turning around on a path and asking you, kindly and directly: what are you looking for? Let the real answer come up, not the one you think you should give: peace, a person, rest, or I don't know, which is an answer too. If you pray, tell God plainly what you're seeking; if you don't, just let yourself hear your own answer.
Agnus Dei. The Latin for Lamb of God, John the Baptist's name for Jesus at the Jordan, sung again at every Mass before Communion. Today's word.
Your line: what seek you. His first question in this Gospel, still asked. That's day four hundred ninety-four.

howItsDone: At every Mass the Lamb of God (Agnus Dei) is sung or said while the priest breaks the host, and just before Communion he holds it up and repeats John the Baptist's words, behold the Lamb of God.

chat.says: Why does the priest say 'Behold the Lamb of God' before Communion?
options: It's John the Baptist's line at the Jordan, pointing to Jesus; the priest points the same way.
It's a line Jesus said about himself at the Last Supper, as he broke the bread.
It's from a prayer the apostles wrote for the first Mass after Jesus rose again.
chat.meaning: In John's Gospel, John the Baptist points at Jesus and says, behold the Lamb of God. The priest lifts the host and points the same way.

Bethania.meaning: a place beyond the Jordan where John baptized

Andrew.meaning: one of the two who followed Jesus that day

tenth hour.meaning: late afternoon, counting the hours from sunrise

Rabbi.meaning: teacher; what the two call Jesus

sources.quoted: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world.

notes: The Mass wording ('behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world') is described from the current Missal and not quoted as a source; the ICEL translation is copyrighted. Confirm the paraphrase is acceptable.

Unnamed disciple as the beloved disciple/the writer: stated as many readers' view since early times. Confirm.
'What seek you?' as Jesus's first words in John: confirm.
